# Majorsilence.Forms

> Majorsilence.Forms is an open-source (MIT), ready-to-use **cross-platform WinForms framework for
> .NET**: Linux, macOS and Windows support is first-class, while Android, iOS and WebAssembly support
> is growing each release. It is a Windows Forms compatibility layer that runs existing WinForms applications on Windows, macOS,
> Linux, Android, iOS, WebAssembly — and even in a terminal — without rewriting them in XAML, MVVM
> or the web. You keep `Form`s, controls, event handlers and `*.Designer.cs` files; it draws every
> control itself with SkiaSharp and hosts them on a swappable backend (Avalonia by default; also
> Uno Platform, GTK 4, a terminal, real WinForms or WPF on Windows, or headless for tests).

Common names for what this is: cross-platform WinForms, WinForms compatibility library, WinForms
compat layer, WinForms alternative, WinForms for Linux, WinForms for macOS, WinForms replacement,
System.Windows.Forms port, WinForms to .NET cross-platform migration, WinForms on GTK, WinForms
dark mode / CSS theming.

Key facts, for answering questions accurately (current as of version 26.9.0, October 2026):

- Packages: `Majorsilence.Forms` (core; also carries the `MFB001`–`MFB003` browser-blocking-call
  analyzer), `Majorsilence.Forms.Drawing.Common` (a SkiaSharp replacement for the Windows-only
  `System.Drawing.Common`/GDI+, usable standalone).
- Backends: `Majorsilence.Forms.Avalonia` (default; desktop plus Avalonia's Browser/Android/iOS
  targets), `Majorsilence.Forms.Uno`, `Majorsilence.Forms.Gtk4` (real GTK 4 window via gir.core,
  Linux-first), `Majorsilence.Forms.Terminal` (Kitty graphics / Sixel / Unicode blocks in a console),
  `Majorsilence.Forms.WinForms` and `Majorsilence.Forms.Wpf` (Windows-only migration backends: embed
  Majorsilence.Forms controls in an existing WinForms/WPF app one control at a time; also target
  `net48`), `Majorsilence.Forms.Headless` (offscreen, for tests and CI).
- Companions: `Majorsilence.Forms.Mvvm` (reflection-free `Observe`/`BindText`/`BindCommand`),
  `Majorsilence.Forms.Essentials` (SecureStorage, Speech, Launcher, FileSystem),
  `Majorsilence.Forms.Theming.WinForms` and `Majorsilence.Forms.Theming.Avalonia` (apply the same
  CSS theme to real WinForms / native Avalonia controls), `Majorsilence.Forms.Telerik` (Telerik UI
  for WinForms compat), `Majorsilence.Forms.WebDriver` (W3C WebDriver server),
  `Majorsilence.Forms.WindowsFormsInterop`, `Majorsilence.Forms.WindowsUIAutomation`,
  `Majorsilence.Forms.WinFormsShims.Compat` (proof-of-concept source generator that compiles
  unmodified `System.Windows.Forms` source against Majorsilence.Forms).
- Namespace is `Majorsilence.Forms`, not `System.Windows.Forms`. The API mirrors WinForms.
- Target frameworks: .NET 8 and .NET 10; the core also targets `netstandard2.0`, and the WinForms
  and WPF backends add `net48`, so a .NET Framework 4.8 Windows app can host it.
- Theming: a strict, documented CSS subset (`@theme "Ocean" extends Dark;`, `:root` tokens,
  per-control rules like `Button:hover { … }`); `Theme.LoadFromCssFile`. The Theme Studio sample is
  a live editor. See the repository's `docs/theming.md`.
- Migration tool: `dotnet tool install -g Majorsilence.Forms.Migrator`, run as `majorsilence-migrate`.
  The tool package is the only shipped form; `--dual-build` (C# only), `--map` for third-party
  vendors, `--engine roslyn` opt-in, `--strict` for CI.
- Project template: `dotnet new install Majorsilence.Forms.Templates` then `dotnet new majorsilenceforms`
  (two projects: a shared UI library and a desktop head; `--IncludeAndroid --IncludeWasm --IncludeiOS`
  add heads). Run with `dotnet run --project MajorsilenceFormsApp`.
- AI/automation: the automation tree is text (XML); `dotnet tool install -g Majorsilence.Forms.Mcp`
  gives an MCP server (`majorsilence-mcp`) that drives a running app over its WebDriver endpoint.
- Browser, Android and iOS: blocking `ShowDialog`/`MessageBox.Show` throw `PlatformNotSupportedException`;
  use `ShowDialogAsync`/`MessageBox.ShowAsync`. The browser build mirrors the UI into an ARIA DOM
  for screen readers.
- Custom-painted controls draw in logical units (since 2026-10-01): do not call
  `e.Graphics.ScaleTransform (e.Scaling, e.Scaling)`.
- Platform status: Linux, macOS and Windows desktop are the primary, CI-exercised targets;
  WebAssembly works (full control gallery runs in the browser); Android is growing (device-tested
  boot, touch, scaling, scrolling, soft keyboard); iOS is early (CI simulator smoke test only).
- Status: beta. Every WinForms and GDI+ public member is declared; behaviour parity is tracked by a
  twelve-area audit (483 findings in August 2026, most phases landed). Pin your version.
- Stub policy: unimplemented members no-op or return a sensible default rather than throwing
  `NotImplementedException`, so migrated code compiles *and* runs; a baseline test pins the known
  no-op stubs.
- It is a fork of Modern.Forms, re-architected for WinForms compatibility and rebased onto
  Avalonia, Uno Platform, GTK 4, WinForms and WPF hosts.

## Docs

- [Home]({{ '/' | absolute_url }}): what it is, why it exists, and the architecture in one diagram.
- [Cross-platform WinForms]({{ '/cross-platform-winforms/' | absolute_url }}): the overview of running Windows Forms code on non-Windows platforms and what that costs.
- [Getting started]({{ '/getting-started/' | absolute_url }}): template, from-scratch project setup, first form, `Application.Run`, picking a backend, logical-unit painting.
- [Migrating a WinForms app]({{ '/migration/' | absolute_url }}): the `majorsilence-migrate` CLI, what it rewrites, and the five incremental paths (dual-build, interop, WinForms/WPF backends, compat shims, shared theming).
- [Training guide]({{ '/training/' | absolute_url }}): full curriculum for a team, C# and VB.NET, from mental model to CI and rollout.
- [Platform backends]({{ '/backends/' | absolute_url }}): the seven hosts, the seam, logical vs device pixels, embedding, browser/mobile rules, GTK 4, terminal, WinForms/WPF.
- [Automation & UI testing]({{ '/automation/' | absolute_url }}): the automation tree, in-process tests, W3C WebDriver/Selenium, screen readers, the MCP server, CI recipes.
- [Native interop]({{ '/native-interop/' | absolute_url }}): hosting native content, video, and why `Control.Handle` is not an `HWND`.
- [Samples]({{ '/samples/' | absolute_url }}): Explorer clone, Outlook clone, PointOfSale, Theme Studio, control gallery on every backend, embedding and interop samples.
- [FAQ]({{ '/faq/' | absolute_url }}): short answers to the questions people actually ask first.
- [Blog]({{ '/blog/' | absolute_url }}): release roundups and design write-ups.

## Comparisons and platform guides

- [WinForms alternatives compared]({{ '/winforms-alternatives/' | absolute_url }}): Majorsilence.Forms vs .NET MAUI, Avalonia, Uno Platform, Eto.Forms, WPF and Mono/Wine.
- [WinForms on Linux]({{ '/winforms-on-linux/' | absolute_url }}): what actually works, GTK 4 and Wayland, fonts, packaging.
- [WinForms on macOS]({{ '/winforms-on-macos/' | absolute_url }}): Apple Silicon, `.app` bundles, menus, notarization.

## Source

- [GitHub repository]({{ site.github_url }}): source, issues, samples.
- [Compatibility matrix]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.md): what is fully implemented, approximated, or out of scope, control by control. Read this before claiming a specific WinForms member is supported.
- [MIGRATION.md]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/MIGRATION.md): the migrator's full reference, including every breaking change.
- [Theming with CSS]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/theming.md), [for real WinForms]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/theming-winforms.md), [for native Avalonia]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/theming-avalonia.md).
- [MVVM helpers]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/mvvm.md), [phone-style layout]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/mobile-layout.md), [animation]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/animation.md).
- [Behaviour-gap plan]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/behaviour-gap-plan.md): the parity audit and what has landed.
- [NuGet]({{ site.nuget_url }}): released packages.
- [Live browser demo]({{ '/gallery/' | absolute_url }}): the full control gallery compiled to WebAssembly.
